newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent edges up after falls, trade very thin.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent edges up after falls, trade very thin.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were slightly firmer on Tuesday but business was very meagre, brokers and traders said.
August Brent, which expires on Wednesday, was four cents a barrel firmer at $17.86 at 0950 GMT, while September was eight cents firmer at $17.94.
"The whole floor activity is absolutely dreadful this morning," one dealer said. "There has not been a decent sized trade one way or the other.
A chart analyst suggested prices may have a slightly firmer tone as a corrective response to sharp falls on Monday.

Those were prompted partly by news out of Baghdad that Iraq and the U.N. had agreed on a food distribution plan, bringing renewed crude oil exports under the country's oil-for-food deal with the U.N. a step nearer.
Confirmation that Germany would sell 2.8 million barrels of oil in early August, as a first tranche of the sale of its strategic oil reserves, provided the market with an additional bearish focus.
Technical analysts pegged nearest support on Tuesday at $17.70, with nearby resistance up at $17.95-$18.
